hook.line: When a bank, a university or a building manager needs something from you, they do not say "can you help?". They have a standard line, and you will see it on every notice.
hook.es: Solicitamos su colaboración para llenar la encuesta.
hook.en: We ask for your help in filling in the survey.

rule:
*Solicitamos su colaboración para…* is how an organisation asks for help: a bank, a school, a building manager.

*Solicitamos* is "we" (the organisation). *Solicito* is "I", one person writing.
*Su* means "your", formal.

Then *para* and an infinitive says what you need: *para llenar el formulario*.

It is the official cousin of *¿me echas una mano?*, which is for friends.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an institutional register formula. *Colaboración* here just means "help", not "collaboration".

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *solicitamos* or *solicito*. A bank writes to its clients: ___ su colaboración para llenar el formulario. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Solicitamos su colaboración para llenar el formulario.
yourTurn.why: A bank is an organisation, so *we*: *solicitamos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *su* or *nuestra*. You write to a client, formal: Solicito ___ colaboración para firmar el contrato. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Solicito su colaboración para firmar el contrato.
yourTurn.why: The help comes from the person you write to, so *su*.

yourTurn.answer: Solicitamos su colaboración para enviar los documentos a tiempo.
yourTurn.why: *Para* and the infinitive say what is needed.

pitfalls.wrong: Solicitamos su colaboración a llenar el formulario.
pitfalls.right: Solicitamos su colaboración para llenar el formulario.
pitfalls.why: Almost. What the help is for is introduced by *para*.

pitfalls.wrong: Solicitamos su colaboración para llenando el formulario.
pitfalls.right: Solicitamos su colaboración para llenar el formulario.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "in filling", but after *para* Spanish uses the infinitive.

pitfalls.wrong: Vale, solicito su colaboración para mover la mesa.
pitfalls.right: Vale, ¿me echas una mano con la mesa?
pitfalls.why: Almost. That formula is stiff for a friend; use *¿me echas una mano?*.

personal: Imagine you run a building or a club and need people's help with one thing. Write the notice: *Solicitamos su colaboración para…*.
